# Audit Skill Improvements: P1–P3 Optimization Backlog

## Problem Statement

The audit skill (`skill/audit/`) has accumulated correctness gaps, performance issues, and code-quality debt from prior feature additions. This epic coordinates the systematic resolution of critical and high-priority defects followed by medium-priority refactors and polish.

## Users

- **Map (agent):** Executes `/skill:audit` on work items and expects fast, correct, reproducible audits.
- **Ralph (orchestrator):** Consumes persisted audit reports (`skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`) to gate merge approvals.
- **Developers:** Review audit output and fix flagged issues; they rely on audit accuracy.

> **User stories (derived from children):**
> 1. As a developer, I want the audit to detect uncommitted working-tree changes so it does not produce stale verdicts.
> 2. As an operator, I want audit `wl` calls to resolve the worklog store efficiently (cached, not per-call sibling scan).
> 3. As an orchestrator, I want the audit SKILL.md to stay under ~13 KB so it fits in context windows.
> 4. As a developer, I want the audit runner to execute faster by avoiding redundant `wl show` fetches and consolidating duplicate parsers.
> 5. As a reviewer, I want the test suite to be split by concern for faster iteration and clearer failure diagnostics.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **All P1 (critical) children are closed:** `SA-0MSL1YWOG005QAH8` (done), `SA-0MSL1YX24000V2MG` (done), `SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ` (done).
2. **All P2 (high) children are closed:** `SA-0MSL1Z15600760KC`, `SA-0MSL1Z1J50038RBF` (done), `SA-0MSL1Z1WU005O5IY`.
3. **All P3 (medium) children are closed:** `SA-0MSL1Z67Z001ZO87`, `SA-0MSL1Z6M7002EDS0`, `SA-0MSL1Z70C007B9VZ`, `SA-0MSL1Z7E9005TLBA`, `SA-0MSL1ZB5J005ENLI`, `SA-0MSL1ZBJO00411KU`, `SA-0MSL1ZBY0007PIVD`.
4. **Full project test suite passes** (`/skill:test`) with no new failures.
5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **No behavioral regression** in the audit verdict (accept/no-accept/timeout) logic — all changes must be verified against existing test coverage.
- **Children must be worked sequentially by priority:** P1 first (critical defects → correctness), then P2 (high → correctness/performance), then P3 (medium → quality/efficiency).
- **All changes in worktrees** per the implement skill — never edit the main checkout directly.
- **SKILL.md must remain under ~13 KB** after restructure (child `SA-0MSL1Z1J50038RBF` already achieved this).

## Existing State

| Area | Current state |
|---|---|
| **SKILL.md** | 12.8 KB (restructured from 44 KB by `SA-0MSL1Z1J50038RBF`) |
| **audit_runner.py** | ~1200-line `cmd_issue()`, 251 tests in monolithic `test_audit_runner.py`, uses `git HEAD sha` + description hash for fingerprint (misses working-tree state) |
| **Worklog-dir resolution** | Cached by `SA-0MSL1YX24000V2MG` |
| **Dead code** | Removed in `SA-0MSL1YWOG005QAH8` |
| **Duplicate parsers** | Consolidated by `SA-0MSL1Z15600760KC` |
| **Pre-flight affirmation** | Documented in SKILL.md, implemented/removed by `SA-0MSL1Z1WU005O5IY` |
| **Duplicated helpers** | `_record_script_failure` closures, `SCANNING` block constant, ISO-8601 freshness timestamp parsing |
| **Redundant fetches** | Multiple `wl show` calls per audit run |
| **Doc drift** | `./scripts/failure_notice.py` path in SKILL.md does not resolve |

## Desired Change

All 13 children (P1→P2→P3) implemented, each delivering its own measurable improvement, resulting in a faster, more correct, and maintainable audit skill.

## Risks & Assumptions

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **P1 bug fix (`SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ`) introduces regressions** | Medium | Preserve existing fingerprint output for git-HEAD-only runs; add regression test covering HEAD-only scenario |
| **`cmd_issue` decomposition (~1200 lines) breaks existing behavior** | High | Extract with zero behavior change; verify via full test suite; commit incrementally |
| **Test split (`SA-0MSL1ZBJO00411KU`) increases maintenance burden** | Low | Split by concern only; maintain one test per logical audit step |
| **P3 children conflict with each other** | Low | Children are independently scoped; verify before implementing |
| **Scope creep — adding improvements beyond the 13 children** | Medium | Record opportunities as new work items; do not add to this epic's scope |

**Assumptions:**
- Each child's acceptance criteria are accurate and testable (verified at child intake)
- The `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` contract does not change during this epic
- All children are independently implementable (no inter-child dependencies beyond priority ordering)

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Operational brief (already restructured to ~12.8 KB)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Core runner (~1200 lines, `cmd_issue()` target for decomposition)
- `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` — Grep-based scanning
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — Audit report persistence
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — 251-test monolith to be split by concern
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — Shared status lifecycle context manager
- `skill/scripts/pi_utils.py` — Pi JSON-stream parser (duplicate + latent bug)
- `skill/scripts/failure_notice.py` — Failure notice template (doc drift fix)
- `skill/audit/tests/` — Test directory to grow with split tests

## Related Work

| Work Item | Title | Stage |
|---|---|---|
| `SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ` | Working-tree state in content fingerprint (stale-audit gap) | done |
| `SA-0MSL1YX24000V2MG` | Cache worklog-dir resolution | done |
| `SA-0MSL1YWOG005QAH8` | Remove/wire discarded Pi model call in cmd_project | done |
| `SA-0MSL1Z1J50038RBF` | Restructure SKILL.md into operational brief + deep docs | done |
| `SA-0MSG48MEI0083K82` | CRITICAL: Audit runner cwd-independence broken | — |
| `SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E` | Audit runner has circular dependency (child blocks parent) | — |
| `SA-0MS3G0D6A009TM81` | Phase 2 code review doesn't always happen | — |

---

## Plan: Changelog

| Time (UTC) | Action |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-13T04:29Z | Plan skill run: 6 automated review stages passed. Recommended execution order updated (test split before decomposition; doc drift fix early). 3 open questions recorded in comments. |

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

No interview questions were asked — the seed context (epic description + 13 children with individual ACs) was sufficient. The plan skill ran 6 automated review stages with findings documented.

**Open Questions (from effort/risk assessment):**

1. Q: Scope of Pre-flight affirmation — implement fully or remove?
   Answer (plan): Recommend implementing lightweight guard (status check + `--force` bypass) rather than full removal, since the documentation exists and a cheap guard adds value.

2. Q: cmd_issue decomposition — how many phases is optimal?
   Answer (plan): 5-6 named phases as suggested in the child AC, operating on a small context dataclass.

3. Q: Test split strategy — by concern, by test type, or by feature?
   Answer (plan): By concern (matches existing split pattern in the audit test directory).
data.title: Audit skill improvements: P1-P3 optimization backlog

# Implement skill: run risk/effort evaluation rather than failing on the gate for plan_complete items missing risk/effort

Companion to ContextHub P4 (WL-0MTTSWCJR003OMN7, RCA WL-0MTTS9FY00055QJV) — related-to: WL-0MTTSWCJR003OMN7 (cross-repo companion, see ContextHub worklog). This is a SorraAgents-tracked work item (skill source lives in `skill/implement/` of this repo, symlinked to `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement`).

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher gates implement dispatch on `open/plan_complete` items having `risk ≤ Medium` and `effort ≤ Medium` (`classifyItemForDispatch` fails closed when risk/effort are absent). Items created without estimates are therefore **never implement-dispatchable** and no mechanism evaluates them (evidence: open_source_llm has 6 of 7 open plan_complete items with empty risk/effort — OSL-0MSG7XUY0009OTVA et al.). The ContextHub dispatcher-side fix (P4) will either dispatch a risk/effort evaluation or adopt a default; either way the **implement skill** must behave correctly when invoked on (or alongside) an item whose estimates are missing — currently the effort/risk gate blocks the run instead of producing the missing data.

## Desired change

In the implement skill (`skill/implement/SKILL.md` and its scripts):
1. When starting implementation of a plan_complete item that lacks risk and/or effort, run the risk/effort evaluation (the effort-and-risk skill — `skill/effort-and-risk`/`effort_and_risk_skill`) **before/at gate time** and persist the estimates on the work item (wl update --risk/--effort), so the item is properly sized and the run proceeds — rather than failing on the gate.
2. Alternatively/additionally: when the dispatcher has already dispatched a standalone risk/effort evaluation for such an item, the implement skill accepts the item once estimates are present (no gate error).
3. Keep the gate for items WITH estimates (no behaviour change there); document the missing-estimate path in the SKILL.md and AGENTS guidance.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Invoking implement on a plan_complete item with empty risk/effort produces and persists risk/effort estimates and proceeds (or cleanly hands off to the evaluation), instead of refusing on the gate.
2. Estimates persist via `wl update` and the item becomes implement-dispatchable by the ContextHub dispatcher afterwards (cross-project fixture/step verified with OSL-0MSG7XUY0009OTVA shape).
3. SKILL.md documents the missing-estimate flow; no regression for items with estimates.
4. Full project suite green (this repo).

## Key files

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (+ `skill/implement/scripts/*`)
- `skill/effort-and-risk` (existing evaluation skill to reuse)

## Related

- ContextHub RCA WL-0MTTS9FY00055QJV and its P4 child (dispatcher-side); open_source_llm items OSL-0MSG7XUY0009OTVA, OSL-0MST3DPNF00812I3, OSL-0MSG7Y9TI000KDUO, OSL-0MSG7YB8U004C1RE, OSL-0MSG7YE3S0021DZT, OSL-0MSG7YFZG007IH3D (evidence)

# Ship skill: parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules for child audits in the final-validation gate

## Problem statement

The ship skill's final-validation gate (Step 6) sweeps ALL `in_review` items — top-level and children — and blocks on any child whose audit is missing/stale/failing. This contradicts Steps 2 (audit readiness) and 5 (producer review), which are deliberately top-level scoped, and the documentation's own statement that "Child items are covered by their parent's audit and never block." The result is that a release can be blocked by child audit gaps that are either already covered by a passing parent audit or outside the release scope.

## Users

- **Release manager:** wants to ship without being blocked by child audit gaps that are already covered by the parent's audit or outside the release scope.
- **Ship skill automation:** needs deterministic rules for child-audit scoping so the release is repeatable without operator intervention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Parent coverage:** the final-validation gate treats a child as `passing` (non-blocking) when its parent (resolved via `parentId`) has a **passing** audit (`readyToClose === true`), and records the coverage in the gate report (e.g. "N child(ren) covered by passing parent audit <parentId>"). The step-2 audit gate is authoritative for top-level readiness, so a passing parent audit covers its children regardless of the conservative time-gate staleness heuristic (operator ruling 2026-09-23: "as long as the parent passes audit then children are assumed to do so").
2. **Out-of-scope exclusion:** the final-validation gate **excludes** a child whose parent is not in stage `in_review` (i.e. the parent is not part of the release) — such children never block, and are reported as excluded with the parent id and stage.
3. **Conservative fallback:** parent coverage does **not** apply when the parent audit is missing, transient, or failing (`readyToClose !== true`). An uncovered child with a missing/stale/failing audit still blocks exactly as today (exit 12). (A passing parent audit covers even when the conservative time-gate would label it stale — the audit's content fingerprint is unchanged and Step 2 already validated readiness.)
4. **Top-level behaviour unchanged:** top-level `in_review` items are evaluated exactly as today; the new rules apply only to children.
5. **Recursion/ancestors:** coverage resolves through the parent chain safely — a child of a child (grandchild) is covered by its nearest `in_review` ancestor with a passing audit; a non-`in_review` ancestor excludes the subtree.
6. **Hermetic unit tests** (injectable boundaries; no live `wl`/`audit_runner`): (a) covered child passes; (b) uncovered child with a failing audit still blocks; (c) child of a non-`in_review` parent is excluded; (d) parent with a stale audit does not cover; (e) grandchild resolves via nearest passing ancestor; (f) a child whose `parentId` references a deleted/non-existent item is handled per AC13 (no crash, deterministic outcome).
7. **Documentation:** `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` describe the parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules and their precedence, so the decision is repeatable without operator intervention.
8. **Exit codes unchanged:** the gate still exits 12 on genuine uncovered failures; successful runs still exit 0.
9. **Scoped close:** the close-work-items step closes only items in the release candidate set (and, when recursing, only descendants that are themselves candidates or are explicitly included) — a `--force` recursive close must not close descendants outside the candidate set. An excluded subtree nested beneath a shipped item survives the release intact.
10. **Collateral detection/report:** the close step reports any descendant it would close outside the candidate set, and any such closure is either refused or recorded as an explicit, reversible exclusion decision.
11. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, SKILL.md, and the ship skill reference docs.
12. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.
13. **Deleted/non-existent parent (orphan) handling:** when a child's `parentId` references a work item that does not exist (deleted), the gate must not crash and must behave deterministically: the orphan is NOT treated as covered (it has no passing parent to inherit from) and is either excluded from the release candidate set with the reason recorded, or evaluated on its own audit — consistent with the Precedence rules. Deleting a parent must not leave its children blocking indefinitely without an explicit, documented outcome.

## Precedence

For each child, evaluate in order:
1. Parent not in `in_review` → **excluded** (not part of the release).
2. Parent (nearest `in_review` ancestor) has a fresh passing audit → **covered/satisfied**.
3. Otherwise → evaluate the child's own audit (missing/stale/transient → auto-remediate; failing → block).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** parent-coverage resolution only applies to `in_review` parents; any further scoping rules (e.g. `completed` status, other stages) are recorded as linked work items, not added here.
- **Circular references:** a work item referencing itself or forming a parent cycle would cause infinite recursion; the implementation must detect and break cycles.
- **Performance:** resolving parent chains for many `in_review` items could be expensive; a bounded parent cache is noted in the implementation plan.
- **Close step regression:** scoping the close step may uncover other subtrees that were previously swept; these should be tested explicitly.

## Constraints

- Changes must not alter the exit-code contract (exit 12 for genuine failures, exit 0 for success).
- Parent-coverage resolution must be bounded (avoid infinite loops in circular references).
- The close-work-items step must not close items outside the candidate set, preserving work in progress on non-release workstreams.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` queries **all** `in_review` items (top-level + children) and blocks on any audit issue.
- Steps 2 and 5 are top-level scoped (`parentId == null`), creating the documented contradiction.
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` close-work-items uses `wl close --force` which recursively closes descendants, including non-candidate subtrees.
- No existing unit tests for `check-final-validation.js`.

## Desired change

- Extend `check-final-validation.js` with parent-coverage + out-of-scope logic.
- Extend `run-release.js` close step with candidate-set scoping.
- Add hermetic unit tests.
- Update `SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — extend with parent-coverage + out-of-scope logic
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — scope close-work-items to candidate set
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — reuse `classifyAudit` / `isAuditStale`
- `skill/ship/tests/` — add unit tests (new file for check-final-validation tests)
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — document parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — document gate scoping rules

## Related work

- **SA-0MU32T8SH001R8MZ** – R4: Prevent concurrency saturation from aborting the Phase 1 parent screen (completed)
- **SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM** – Audit staleness race: post-persist comment bumps updatedAt past auditedAt — passed audits show stale icon (completed)
- **SA-0MSGAUD3H007P8Y4** – P5: test _deep_analyze_child retry forwarding + timeout-default AC clarification (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions asked — the work item is sufficiently defined by the discovery context (TCE release 2026-09-15) and the operator's ruling recorded in the discovery comment.

## Appendix: v0.1.17 release findings (2026-09-23)

Observed during the `/skill:ship release` attempt that was blocked at Step 6 (final-validation gate, exit 12), after Steps 2 (audit readiness) and 5 (producer review) passed:

- **Scale:** the gate swept **104 `in_review` items**; **52** lacked a passing audit. Most were children whose parents had passed audit — exactly the case AC1/AC2 address.
- **Deleted parent (NEW edge case):** parent `SA-0MSRVN28E009OL5S` had been **deleted**, yet its **5 children** (`SA-0MSRVXECH0019962`, `SA-0MSRW9BV20029XEB`, `SA-0MSRW9FS0006CUYJ`, `SA-0MSRWB5LM0057VQ9`, `SA-0MSRWB1V7006IEW3`) remained `in_review` and blocked the gate. Deleting the parent did **not** stop its children from blocking. This is the case AC13 adds.
- **Transient infrastructure interaction:** one orphan (`SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB`) could not be re-audited (`Pi provider error: Connection error.`, ~713 s) due to a stale-ctx exception in the `proxy-compaction-bridge` extension — see SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F. It was manually deleted by the operator to proceed. This reinforces that a child blocked only by a transient/provider error must not hard-block the release.
- **Documentation contradiction confirmed:** `skill/ship/SKILL.md` Step 6 currently states the gate is "deliberately **not** top-level-scoped", which is the opposite of the operator's ruling that children are covered by a passing parent (AC1/AC2/AC7/AC11 must correct this text).
- **Operator ruling (2026-09-23):** "Step 6 should be top level only. As long as the parent passes audit then children are assumed to do so."

# Objective

Interview-driven skills (intake, plan) must require the agent to state its **preferred option explicitly** — with a short rationale — for every clarifying question/round, so operators can accept a recommendation at a glance instead of evaluating bare option lists.

## Problem statement

Agents running the interview-driven skills (`intake`, `plan`) ask clarifying questions and present options, but the skills never require the agent to say which option it prefers. Operators must therefore assess every option themselves and frequently reply "what do you recommend?", adding round-trips. The agent's reasoning is also left implicit. Requiring an explicit preferred option (clearly marked as a recommendation) makes interviews faster and keeps the agent's reasoning visible, without removing the operator's choice.

## Users

AI agents conducting interviews, and producers/operators answering them.

**User stories:**

- As a producer answering an intake or plan interview, I want the agent to tell me which option it prefers and why, so that I can accept it immediately or override it with full context.
- As an AI agent following the skill instructions, I want one explicit rule on how to phrase recommendations, so that I apply it consistently in every interview round.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/intake/SKILL.md` (Interview section and interview-style hard requirement) requires the agent to state its preferred option for each interview question/round, using a consistent marker such as `**Recommended:** <option> — <one-line rationale>`.
2. `skill/plan/SKILL.md` (Interview section and interview-style hard requirement) states the same requirement with the same marker.
3. The wording makes clear the recommendation is **advisory**: the operator may choose any option, and the agent proceeds with the operator's choice (no unilateral selection and no auto-selecting the recommendation without confirmation).
4. The requirement applies to every interview round and to the producer-review handoff (questions routed via `wl reviewed`), not only the first round.
5. A doc-hygiene test asserts the recommendation requirement is present in both skill docs (e.g. `tests/test_interview_recommendation.py` asserting the marker/instruction text in both `SKILL.md` files).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline (`skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js`). Implementing agents should not manually update CHANGELOG.md.

## Constraints

- Scope is skill markdown plus one doc-hygiene test; no changes to `wl`, runtime scripts, or work-item data.
- Must not conflict with `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`, which explicitly forbids asking the user what to refactor — refactor is not an interview skill and is out of scope.
- Wording must stay concise and consistent with the existing style of both skills (short bullets, no new sub-structures).
- The consolidation of interview conduct into a shared interview skill is tracked separately as **SA-0MUBVM6FR000NDI1**; this item must deliver the behaviour without waiting for that refactor.

## Existing state

- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` § "Hard requirements" has "Interview style: concise, high-signal questions, max three per round." and § "4. Interview" describes the interview loop — neither requires an explicit recommendation.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` § "Hard requirements" has "Use concise interview style: ≤3 high-signal questions per iteration; prefer multiple-choice but allow freeform." and § "3. Interview" — neither requires an explicit recommendation.
- There is **no** shared interview skill or module: no `skill/interview/` directory, and no `interview`/`Interview` class or function in `skill/shared/` (interviews are agent-driven prose, not scripted).

## Desired change

1. In `skill/intake/SKILL.md`:
   - Add to the interview-style hard requirement: the agent must state its preferred option explicitly (with a one-line rationale) for every question/round, marked `**Recommended:**`.
   - Reinforce in § "4. Interview" that the recommendation is advisory and the operator's choice always wins.
2. In `skill/plan/SKILL.md`:
   - Apply the identical requirement to the interview-style hard requirement and § "3. Interview".
3. Add a doc-hygiene test asserting both skill docs contain the recommendation requirement.

## Key Files:

- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Add the explicit-preferred-option rule to the interview-style hard requirement and the § 4 Interview section.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Add the same rule to the interview-style hard requirement and the § 3 Interview section.
- `tests/test_interview_recommendation.py` — New doc-hygiene test asserting the recommendation requirement text appears in both `SKILL.md` files.
- `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` — Reflect the interview-conduct requirement if maintainer-facing reference detail is added.
- `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` — Same for the plan skill.

## Related work

### Potentially related work items

- **SA-0MUBVM6FR000NDI1** — "Refactor intake and plan to share a common interview skill" (`open`, high): the separate refactor item requested alongside this one; consolidates the interview conduct that this item amends.
- **SA-0MRIIQLQ800788MC** — "Refactor command/intake.md for conciseness" (`completed`): previous pass over intake interview guidance.
- **SA-0MS3CIU0F00066CD** — "Move /intake command to be a skill" (`completed`): established `skill/intake/SKILL.md` as the live interview process.
- **SA-0MRW7ER4L000SK8Z** — "Shared status lifecycle helper for skills" (`completed`): precedent for extracting shared skill behaviour into `skill/shared/`.

### Potentially related docs

- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — the intake interview process.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — the plan interview process.

# Objective

Extract a single canonical interview skill that `intake` and `plan` both reference for interview conduct, removing the duplicated interview prose that currently drifts between the two skills.

## Problem statement

There is no common interview skill. `skill/intake/SKILL.md` (§ 4 Interview) and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` (§ 3 Interview) each define their own interview process in prose, duplicating guidance on question limits (≤3 per round), multiple-choice preference, producer-review handoff (`wl reviewed`), and appendix recording. Every enhancement must be applied twice and can silently diverge — the preferred-option rule added by **SA-0MUBVLFP70064SPJ** is the most recent example.

## Users

Skill maintainers and the AI agents that execute the intake and plan interviews.

**User stories:**

- As a skill maintainer, I want one canonical definition of interview conduct, so that I can change it once and both skills pick it up.
- As an AI agent running an interview, I want a single unambiguous interview contract to follow, so that my behaviour is identical in intake and plan.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A canonical interview component exists (proposed: `skill/interview/SKILL.md`, marked `disable-model-invocation: true`), defining at minimum: ≤3 high-signal questions per round, multiple-choice preferred with freeform allowed, the explicit `**Recommended:** <option>` preferred-option rule (from SA-0MUBVLFP70064SPJ), the producer-review handoff via `wl reviewed`, and idempotent appendix recording of questions/answers.
2. `skill/intake/SKILL.md` and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` reference the shared component instead of restating the interview rules, with no duplication left behind.
3. No interview behaviour is lost or changed beyond consolidation: the requirements listed in AC #1 remain enforced through the shared component.
4. A test asserts both skills reference the shared component and that the shared component contains each required interview rule.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline (`skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js`). Implementing agents should not manually update CHANGELOG.md.

## Constraints

- Follow existing skill-authoring conventions: YAML frontmatter, `$(skill_path <name>)` runtime resolution, and `docs/dev/<skill>-reference.md` for deep reference detail.
- Do not break the scripts/import conventions documented in `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md`.
- Recommended ordering: complete **SA-0MUBVLFP70064SPJ** first so the shared component captures the preferred-option rule; this item is a consolidation, not a behaviour redesign.
- Keep the shared component prose-only unless duplicated runtime logic is found; if constants are needed, place them in `skill/shared/` per existing convention.

## Existing state

- No `skill/interview/` directory exists.
- No `interview`/`Interview` symbol exists in `skill/shared/`; interviews are agent-driven prose, not scripted.
- Interview prose is duplicated in `skill/intake/SKILL.md` § 4 and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` § 3, plus interview-style bullets in each skill's Hard requirements section.

## Desired change

1. Create `skill/interview/SKILL.md` as the canonical interview contract (hidden helper skill).
2. Replace the duplicated interview prose in `skill/intake/SKILL.md` and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` with a reference to the shared component, retaining only skill-specific interview inputs (e.g. seed context, what to capture per feature).
3. Add a test asserting the shared component exists, is referenced by both skills, and contains the required rules.
4. Update maintainer docs.

## Key Files:

- `skill/interview/SKILL.md` — New canonical interview conduct (question limits, multiple-choice preference, explicit preferred-option recommendation, producer-review handoff, appendix recording).
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Replace duplicated interview prose with a reference to the shared component.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Replace duplicated interview prose with a reference to the shared component.
- `tests/test_interview_skill_shared.py` — New test asserting the shared component exists, both skills reference it, and required rules are present.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` — Reference the new skill if path-resolution conventions are affected.

## Related work

### Potentially related work items

- **SA-0MUBVLFP70064SPJ** — "Interview skills must state the agent's preferred option explicitly" (`open`, high): the behaviour change this refactor must preserve; recommended as the predecessor work.
- **SA-0MRW7ER4L000SK8Z** — "Shared status lifecycle helper for skills" (`completed`): precedent and pattern for extracting shared skill behaviour.
- **SA-0MRIIQLQ800788MC** — "Refactor command/intake.md for conciseness" (`completed`): previous consolidation of intake interview guidance.
- **SA-0MS3CIU0F00066CD** — "Move /intake command to be a skill" (`completed`): established the skill-based interview process.

### Potentially related docs

- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` — skill path/import conventions.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — the two duplicated interview definitions.
- `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` — maintainer reference detail.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MTC5CRVI008RD1K** – implement skill report script path is broken (open)
- **SA-0MQUQZMWB0067UCR** – PlanAll: claim command fails due to stage/status validation in wl (completed)
- **SA-0MPAW77DY002QSP4** – /plan should always make tests the first task (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: canonical, choice, common, component, define (+29 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: canonical, common, component, define, duplicated (+25 more)
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — matched: appendix, canonical, choice, define, exists (+25 more)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** Behavioural regression during extraction (a rule dropped or weakened). Mitigation: AC #3 and AC #4 assert rules survive; run both skills' existing tests.
- **Risk:** Scope creep into redesigning interviews while consolidating. Mitigation: consolidation only — no new interview semantics beyond preserving SA-0MUBVLFP70064SPJ.
- **Risk:** A shared skill could be over-abstracted if intake/plan interview needs genuinely diverge. Mitigation: share only the common conduct rules, keep skill-specific capture fields local.
- **Assumption:** A prose shared skill (not a runtime module) is the right granularity, because interviews are agent-driven rather than scripted.
- **Assumption:** Priority `high` per the operator's `--priority high` directive.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked. The operator's seed intent — "Do the skills use a common interview skill? If not create a separate work item to refactor them so they share a common interview skill" — was specific. Repo investigation confirmed no shared interview skill exists (no `skill/interview/`, no shared interview module), so this item was created as instructed.

Decision taken with the operator's stated recommendation:

- **Ordering — Recommended:** complete SA-0MUBVLFP70064SPJ before this item, so the shared component captures the preferred-option rule in one pass. Rationale: avoids implementing the rule twice and then moving it.

# Ship report to Discord needs titling

## Problem statement

The Discord ship report embed title is hardcoded as `Release vX.Y.Z` and does not include the project name from the worklog config. Additionally, the report description should include the project name for clarity.

## Users

- **Release operator**: Wants the Discord notification to clearly identify which project is being released, especially when monitoring multiple project releases.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The Discord embed title changes from `Release vX.Y.Z` to `<ProjectName> Release vX.Y.Z`, where `<ProjectName>` is read from the worklog config's `projectName` field.
2. The project name is resolved from `<project>/.worklog/config.yaml` (same config path used for webhook URL resolution), with fallback to the global config `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`.
3. If the config is missing or `projectName` is absent, the title gracefully falls back to `Release vX.Y.Z`.
4. The embed description includes the project name alongside the version for added clarity.
5. All existing unit tests pass, with updated assertions reflecting the new title format.

## Constraints

- Non-breaking change — existing webhook behaviour must not be affected.
- The YAML parser (`parseSimpleYaml`) already handles top-level `projectName` keys.
- Must use the same config resolution precedence as the webhook URL (project config first, then global).

## Existing state

- `buildDiscordPayload()` in `discord-notify.js` hardcodes the title: `title: Release v${versionText}`.
- The `parseSimpleYaml()` function already parses `projectName` from config (verified in tests).
- `resolveDiscordWebhookUrl()` already follows the correct precedence pattern.
- The `sendReleaseNotification()` function resolves the webhook URL but does not read `projectName`.

## Desired change

1. Add a `resolveProjectName(projectRoot)` helper (parallel to `resolveDiscordWebhookUrl`) that reads `projectName` from the worklog config.
2. Update `sendReleaseNotification()` to resolve the project name and pass it to `buildDiscordPayload()`.
3. Update `buildDiscordPayload()` to accept a `projectName` parameter and include it in the embed title and description.

## Key Files

- `scripts/discord-notify.js` — Add project name resolution and update payload builder
- `tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` — Update title assertions from `Release v1.2.3` to `<ProjectName> Release v1.2.3`

## Related work

- `WL-0MUB023JP001A9N3` — This work item itself (ship skill Discord notification)

## Note on bot name

The "bot name" that appears in Discord messages is controlled by the webhook URL configuration within Discord's channel settings, not by application code. This cannot be fixed programmatically — it requires configuring the webhook's display name in Discord. The fix addresses what CAN be controlled: the embed title and description content.

# live-repo mutation guard false-positives when the suite runs inside an agent worktree

`discovered-from:SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0`

## Problem statement

When the full test suite runs **inside an agent worktree** (the normal `implement.py finish` and `/skill:test` case), the live-repo mutation guard anchors its agent-worktree exclusion on the *passed root* rather than the **main checkout**. Inside a linked worktree that root is the worktree itself, so `excluded_refs` is always empty and any concurrent agent committing to another worktree is reported as a mutation — failing the run and blocking the full-suite release gate for every agent whenever the shared host has more than one active session.

## Users

- **Primary:** AI agents running `/skill:test` or `implement.py finish` from inside an `implement` worktree on a shared multi-agent host.
- **Secondary:** the human producer relying on the full-suite exit code as the pre-push release gate.
- **Tertiary:** maintainers of the shared `git_sandbox.py` helper and the two guards that consume it.

Example user stories:

- As an **implementing agent**, I want the full suite to run green inside my worktree even while sibling agents commit to theirs, so that concurrent sessions do not block my release gate.
- As a **producer**, I want the guard to keep failing on genuine in-place mutation of the guarded checkout, so that real corruption (the `GIT_DIR` incident, SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX) is never reported as green.
- As a **maintainer**, I want one shared fix in `git_sandbox.py`, so the outer `run_tests.py` guard and the inner `live_repo_guard.py` conftest guard cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `snapshot_repo_state()` called with a **linked-worktree root** returns `excluded_refs` containing every branch checked out in a registered worktree under the **main checkout's** `.worklog/worktrees/` (not `<passed_root>/.worklog/worktrees`). Verification: a unit test creates a main repo plus an agent worktree, calls `snapshot_repo_state(worktree_root)`, and asserts the agent worktree's `refs/heads/wl-*` is in `excluded_refs`.
- [ ] **No false positive:** with the guard/snapshot armed at a linked-worktree root, advancing a branch checked out in a *sibling* agent worktree produces `diff_snapshots(before, after)["changed"] == False` and does not fail the guard. Verification: a nested-pytest test that arms the guard inside a worktree, commits in a sibling worktree, and asserts exit code 0 with no `live-repo mutation` text (red on the pre-fix helper).
- [ ] **No false negative:** an in-place mutation of the guarded checkout is still reported — (a) moving `HEAD`/the guarded branch ref, (b) modifying a tracked file, (c) adding an untracked non-ignored file. Verification: the existing `TestSnapshotContract` cases still pass when the guard is armed at a worktree root.
- [ ] **Worktree registration churn does not fail:** registering or removing a worktree under `<main_checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/` during a guarded run does not fail the guard when the reportable diff is empty. Verification: a unit test where `excluded_refs` grows but `diff_snapshots` reports `changed == False` asserts the per-test guard does not fail.
- [ ] **Single shared fix:** both the `run_tests.py` outer guard (`_detect_live_repo_mutation`) and the conftest inner guard (`live_repo_guard.py`) exhibit the corrected behaviour, with the anchoring logic living only in `git_sandbox.py`. Verification: code review plus the guard-level nested-pytest tests.
- [ ] A regression test reproduces the reported failure (red against the pre-fix helper) and passes after the fix, covering the `wl-SA-0MUD5R5EQ...-fix-inherited-pass...` worktree scenario and the observed `moved ref refs/heads/wl-*` suite failures.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. This includes the `git_sandbox.py` module docstring's exclusion-derivation note and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` must remain **stdlib-only** and loadable by file location — the repo-root `conftest.py` loads it via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` and must not mutate `sys.path`.
- Agent-worktree exclusion must be **derived from git plumbing** (e.g. `git worktree list --porcelain`, or `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` to locate the main checkout) — **never** a `wl-*` name pattern. The module docstring documents why: a name pattern would also exclude the incident's own fixture branches and destroy detection of the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX class of bug.
- Snapshots stay **read-only**: only plumbing commands; never `gc`, `update-index`, `fetch`, or `--refresh`.
- The fix must not weaken genuine mutation detection (moved `dev`, config rewrites, tracked/untracked file changes).
- Any extra git invocation per snapshot must be cheap and confined to the snapshot path; it must not turn the per-test fingerprint into a full `status` scan.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::_parse_worktrees` computes `agent_root = root.joinpath(*AGENT_WORKTREE_DIR)`, where `root` is the passed root (for `snapshot_repo_state`, the `git_toplevel(resolved)` of the passed path).
- Reproduced 2026-09-26 on `dev @ 10995367`:
  - `snapshot_repo_state(".")` from the **main checkout** → `excluded_refs` contains all 12 agent-worktree branches.
  - `snapshot_repo_state(".")` from `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSRN0Q64005YR5A-stale-pytest-exit` → `git_toplevel` is the worktree root and `excluded_refs == set()`.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` arms with `root` from `_default_root(config)` (or the repo-root conftest's `_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent`, which inside a worktree is the worktree root).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_detect_live_repo_mutation` calls `snapshot_repo_state(project_root)` where `project_root` comes from `detect_project_root()` (worktree root when run inside one). It shares the same helper and the same defect.
- Adjacent defect (same guard path, reproduced): `fingerprint()` includes `tuple(sorted(excluded))`, and `pytest_runtest_teardown` fails whenever the fingerprint differs — regardless of `diff_snapshots(...)["changed"]`. Adding a second worktree under `.worklog/worktrees/` mid-run changes `excluded` while the diff stays clean, so worktree registration churn is a second false positive.
- Existing tests only arm the guard at the **main** root (`tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py::TestLiveRepoGuard::test_agent_worktree_churn_does_not_trip_the_guard` creates the worktree under the root it arms), so they do not exercise the linked-worktree case.

Minimal reproduction (from any linked worktree):

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents")
from skill.shared import git_sandbox as gs
snap = gs.snapshot_repo_state(".")
print(snap["root"], len(snap["worktrees"]), snap["excluded_refs"])
PY
# from a worktree: excluded_refs == set()  (bug)
# from the main checkout: excluded_refs has every agent-worktree branch
```

## Desired change

- Add a small helper that resolves the **main checkout root** from git plumbing (first entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`, or the parent of `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`), and anchor agent-worktree exclusion on `<main_checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/` rather than the passed root.
- Thread that anchor through `_parse_worktrees` / `snapshot_repo_state`. When the passed root *is* the main checkout the behaviour is unchanged; when it is a linked worktree the exclusion set is now populated correctly.
- Make the per-test guard fail only when `diff_snapshots` reports a reportable change (or exclude the `excluded`-set churn from the fingerprint), so worktree registration/deregistration is not a false positive while the authoritative full diff still catches real mutations.
- Add regression tests at both levels (helper and guard) and document the main-checkout anchoring in the module docstring and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — Add a main-checkout resolver and change `_parse_worktrees`/`snapshot_repo_state` to anchor `agent_root` on `<main_checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/`; address `fingerprint()`/`diff_snapshots` treatment of the excluded set. Module docstring's exclusion-derivation note needs updating.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — `pytest_runtest_teardown` must fail only when the authoritative diff is non-empty (not merely when the cheap fingerprint moves); affects `__init__`, `pytest_runtest_teardown`, `pytest_sessionfinish`.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` — Add `snapshot_repo_state(worktree_root)` exclusion test, sibling-churn no-false-positive test, in-place mutation still-reported test, and excluded-set-churn test (class `TestAgentWorktreeExclusion`).
- `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` — Add a nested-pytest test that arms the guard from inside a linked worktree and commits in a sibling worktree (exit 0, no `live-repo mutation` text); keep the existing main-root test.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Verify `_detect_live_repo_mutation` benefits from the shared fix; add a focused test if the outer guard needs its own coverage.
- `conftest.py` — Confirm the repo-root conftest continues to arm the guard correctly from a worktree (helper-side fix preferred over conftest change).
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — Document main-checkout anchoring and the two false-positive classes.
- `skill/shared/tests/` / `tests/` — New regression tests; `tests/fixtures/` or helper fixtures if a nested-worktree harness is needed.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the operator intends the anchor fix (AC1–AC3, AC5) as the core scope; the worktree-registration churn (AC4) is included because it is the same guard code path and the same symptom class. If the producer prefers, AC4 can be split into a follow-up work item — recorded here rather than silently dropped.
- **Risk (implementation):** relying on `git worktree list --porcelain` ordering (main worktree first) is documented git behaviour but somewhat implicit; prefer `--git-common-dir` or validate the first entry to avoid a fragile assumption.
- **Risk (regression / security):** an incorrect anchor could over- or under-exclude and either mask the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX incident or keep the false positive. Mitigated by AC3 (no false negative) and the existing contract tests.
- **Risk (scope creep):** expanding into a general refactor of the guard. Recorded mitigation: keep changes surgical to the anchoring + fingerprint decision and link any extra opportunity as a separate work item.
- **Risk (performance):** the extra main-root resolution must be cached per snapshot so the per-test fingerprint stays cheap.
- **Risk (test flakiness):** the nested-pytest tests must remain hermetic under `tmp_path` (use the existing `git_sandbox` factories, never the live checkout).

## Related work

- `SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ` — repo-root conftest live-repo guard (introduced the inner guard).
- `SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H` — `run_tests.py` live-repo snapshot guard (the outer guard that shares the helper).
- `SA-0MUG30IIR00978CW` — hermetic git sandbox helper and migration (owns `git_sandbox.py`).
- `SA-0MUG30HV8004HV94` — guard contract tests and guard-fires proof.
- `SA-0MUG30KEV006RBAM` — document hermetic-git requirement and guard.
- `SA-0MUH5KFDV002ORSS` — live-repo guard teardown ordering (adjacent `live_repo_guard.py` defect; shows the same test file is the home for guard regressions).
- `SA-0MUH1MJL6003767Q` — `implement.py run_tests` bypasses `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` (adjacent guard-activation defect; not blocking, but touching the same guard read-path).
- `SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX` — leaked `GIT_DIR` incident (the guard's reason to exist; must stay detected).
- `SA-0MU89WA740004GOJ` — destructive `init` commit wiped repo on `dev` (test-isolation incident context).
- `SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF` — multi-agent audit/test coordination (the contention context that makes this reproducible).
- `SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0` — audit-runner pre-review bypass (source item; `discovered-from`).
- `SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63` — remote `dev` corruption / test isolation (origin of `git_sandbox.py` and the snapshot design).
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — incident write-up and guarded-worktree proof; documents the snapshot/exclusion contract.
- `docs/dev/repro_live_repo_leak.py` — reproduction harness for the leak class the guard protects.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was required: the seed context (`discovered-from:SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0`) already contained the problem, root-cause pointer, expected behaviour, measurable ACs, and related work, and the defect was reproduced directly during intake. Questions below were resolved by repo investigation and recorded for auditability.

- Q: "Is `excluded_refs` really empty when the guard runs inside a linked worktree?" — Answer (agent, repo investigation): Yes. `snapshot_repo_state(".")` from `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSRN0Q64005YR5A-stale-pytest-exit` returned `excluded_refs == set()`, while the same call from the main checkout returned 12 agent-worktree refs. Evidence: `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::_parse_worktrees` (`agent_root = root.joinpath(*AGENT_WORKTREE_DIR)`) and the 2026-09-26 reproduction on `dev @ 10995367`.
- Q: "Does `run_tests.py`'s outer guard share the same defect?" — Answer (agent, repo investigation): Yes. `_detect_live_repo_mutation` calls `snapshot_repo_state(project_root)` and `diff_snapshots`, both from the shared helper; the conftest guard does the same. Evidence: `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`, `conftest.py`.
- Q: "Is there an adjacent false positive from concurrent worktree registration/deregistration?" — Answer (agent, repo investigation): Yes. `fingerprint()` includes `tuple(sorted(excluded))` and `pytest_runtest_teardown` fails on any fingerprint change, so registering a second worktree mid-run fails the guard even though `diff_snapshots` reports `changed == False`. Reproduced with a temp repo: adding `wl-two` changed the fingerprint while the diff stayed clean. Assumed in scope (AC4) as the same guard path; flagged for producer confirmation.
- Q: "Should the fix change the root the conftest/`run_tests.py` pass in, or the helper?" — Answer (agent, decision): the **helper** (`git_sandbox.py`) so both guards benefit and cannot drift (AC5). The passed root may legitimately be a worktree; the helper must resolve the main checkout itself.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MKXYO42T0FC6IJR** – Isolated work environments for parallel work (completed)
- **SA-0MRNW4BN70084S84** – [test-failure] test_other_stages_ask_only_when_genuinely_unclear — failing test (completed)
- **SA-0MSLLGDW00098UCC** – audit_runner: git file-scope/HEAD resolution is cwd-dependent despite cwd-independence claims (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance (+335 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance (+309 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: ac3, ac4, acceptance, acs, active (+267 more)

question: GATING — cannot implement SA-0MUINEW6X0034C65 independently; its blocking fix SA-0MUILGH5E007X627 is parked at a producer approval gate.

## What I verified this session (2026-09-26, dev @ 9c9a1c18)

- `skill/shared/tests/test_queue.py::test_remove_takes_specific_item_only` **passes in isolation** (1 passed in 0.53s) — the named test is not itself defective.
- The live-repo guard false positive is still present and deterministic (helper-level reproduction against the current `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`):
  - `fingerprint differs: True`
  - `diff_snapshots(...)["changed"]: False`
  - `describe_diff(...)`: `  (no differences)`
- Root cause confirmed unchanged: `fingerprint()` returns `(refs-minus-excluded, config, sorted(excluded_refs))`, so agent-worktree registration/removal churn changes the fingerprint, while `diff_snapshots()` filters `excluded_refs` out of every category. `pytest_runtest_teardown` fails on any fingerprint movement without checking `diff_snapshots(...)["changed"]`.

## Why I cannot proceed

- This item is blocked by SA-0MUILGH5E007X627 (`in-progress`, `intake_complete`, `needsProducerReview=true`, assignee Map). Its plan explicitly concluded: "do **not** decompose or implement this item independently … this item should be closed once that fix lands" — the fix must live in the shared `git_sandbox.py`/`live_repo_guard.py` so both guard consumers cannot drift.
- SA-0MUILGH5E007X627 is itself paused pending producer input (it is High risk, so the plan-approval gate fired). Its two OPEN questions are recorded on that item:
  1. Approve the proposed 7-feature decomposition (recommended: (a) approve as-is)?
  2. Keep AC4 (worktree registration churn) in scope for F4/F5, or split it into a follow-up work item (recommended: (a) keep in scope)?

## Decision needed from the producer

Please pick one:

- **(A)** Answer SA-0MUILGH5E007X627 questions 1 and 2 so that blocker can be implemented; then close this item once the fix lands and the test stays green under concurrent worktree churn (the planned path).
- **(B)** Authorise implementing the shared guard fix directly under **SA-0MUINEW6X0034C65** (contrary to the blocked-by plan), i.e. make `pytest_runtest_teardown` fail only on `diff_snapshots(...)["changed"]` and stop folding `sorted(excluded_refs)` into `fingerprint()`, with helper- and guard-level regression tests here. The blocker can then be reconciled as duplicate/superseded.
- **(C)** Some other resolution (e.g. reassign, re-scope, or split).

No code was changed and no worktree was created; the item remains `blocked`. `needsProducerReview` has been set.
